faq: What does this tool calculate?
The integer tile x and y for a latitude/longitude at a zoom, by the standard slippy-map formulas — x from longitude linearly, y from latitude through the Mercator function.
Which map standard does it use?
The OSM/Google slippy-map convention (Web Mercator, 256-px tiles) that effectively all web maps share.
Can I use this in production GIS?
The formula is the production standard — identical to what tile libraries compute. Cache policies and tile-server usage rules are the operational layer on top.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84, the frame web maps and GPS share — tile and pixel systems on this page are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — pixels and tiles quantise the world; extra coordinate decimals beyond the cell size are decoration.
Latitude limits?
Web Mercator caps at ±85.0511° — beyond it there are no tiles, only ice and honesty. The calculator respects the cap.
TMS versus XYZ?
TMS flips y. If your stack is TMS, flip y as (2^z − 1 − y) — the calculator speaks XYZ, the web's majority dialect.
Fractional tile position?
Where inside the tile the point falls is the Map Tile Pixel Offset Calculator's job — this page names the tile.
Antimeridian points?
Longitude wraps: x computes modulo the grid width, and tile sets crossing the seam need the wrap handled — flagged here rather than hidden.
Tile URLs?
https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png is the canonical shape — respect the tile usage policy of whichever server you fetch from.
